row_subject: Samoan affairs: Report of the Secretary of State on the general act signed at Berlin, June 14, 1889. Resumption of the conference of 1887 set forth in correspondence sent to Congress by President Cleveland in February, 1889, and later, reasons were given by President Cleveland for leaving appointment of commissioners to the conference to the incoming administration. The commissioners named; recital of the powers and instructions in general. Five specific heads of instruction: 1. Restoration of the status quo. 2. Organization of a stable governmental system for the islands. 3. Adjustment of claims to and titles of lands. 4. Prohibition or regulation of the importation and sale of fire-arms and alcoholic liquors. 5. The position of the municipal administration of Apia left to the commissioners to decide at the conference, with reference to the promotion of peace and order by maintaining a neutral territory in and about Apia. The conference met at Berlin and held nine formal sittings, the results of which were embodied in the general act or protocol. Views of the powers declared as to, 1. Independence and neutrality of the islands of Samoa, peace and equal rights for foreign residents. 2. Modification of existing treaties, and assent of the Samoan government to the general act. 3. Supreme Court of Justice for Samoa. 4. Land titles. 5. Municipal administration of Apia. 6. Taxation and revenue in Samoa. 7. Restriction of traffic in firearms and intoxicants. The three points most difficult of agreement—discussion of the causes of difference. Incloses the general act and copy of a note from the German minister of June 29, 1889.

As a matter of policy Department desires to announce immediately $5,000,000 credit established in favor of Liberia; necessary inquiries being made as to validity of such obligations of Liberia as may be required; encloses Department memorandum showing financial status of Liberia.
head: The Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury (McAdoo)
note: The Secretary of State's letter of September 9, 1918 to Mr. McAdoo inside Mr. Leffingwell's letter of August 27. The reply has no file number of its own: the shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Financial affairs. refers to desire of French Government for joint representations regarding bank of issue; requests views on measures considered advisable for the United States to take.
head: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Mexico (Fletcher)
note: The Secretary of State's telegram No. 925 of March 28, 1918 to Ambassador Fletcher inside the French ambassador's note of March 16. The reply has no file number of its own: the shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Protection of American oil interests. Instruction to bring situation in Tampico oil fields to attention of Mexican Government and request protection of American life and property.
head: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Mexico (Fletcher)

row_subject: Claims of American citizens against Mexico. Instruction to press Mexican Government for favorable reply to representations made regarding claims commission.

head: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Mexico (Fletcher)

row_subject: Protection of American oil interests. Instruction as to form of protest against bill approving petroleum decrees.
head: The Acting Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Mexico (Fletcher)
note: The Acting Secretary's telegram No. 1740 of December 21, 1918 to Ambassador Fletcher inside the ambassador's telegram of December 16. The reply has no file number of its own: the shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Same subject. Announces appointment of Mr. A. F. Lindberg, as American member of High Commission, and Professor Jenks as umpire; instructions to cable results of reports of Debt Commission, and advice as to exact sum in hands of Nicaraguan Government to pay all claims.
head: The Secretary of State to the Minister in Nicaragua (Jefferson)
note: The Secretary of State's telegram of January 14, 1918 to Minister Jefferson inside the minister's telegram of January 8. The reply has no file number of its own: the shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Same subject. Procedure for transfer of treaty moneys and customs revenues to the High Commission for payment of awards of Commission on Public Credit.
head: The Secretary of State to the Minister in Nicaragua (Jefferson)
note: The Secretary of State's telegram of April 19, 1918 to Minister Jefferson inside the minister's telegram of April 5. The reply has no file number of its own: the shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Convention Prolonging the Armistice With Germany Agreement providing that the Germans shall cease hostilities against the Poles at once and that the armistice with Germany shall be prolonged for a short period, the Allied and Associated Powers reserving to themselves the right to terminate the period at three days’ notice.
head: Convention Prolonging the Armistice With Germany, Signed February 16, 1919
note: The convention of February 16, 1919 prolonging the armistice inside the armistice of November 11, 1918, after the prolongations of December 13 and January 16: the armistice's head carries one source note for all three, and the list gives each a row of its own.

row_subject: Military Convention Between the Allies and Hungary, Signed at Belgrade Regulating conditions under which the armistice between the Allies and Austria-Hungary is to be applied in Hungary.
head: Military Convention Between the Allies and Hungary, Signed at Belgrade, November 13, 1918
note: The military convention signed at Belgrade on November 13, 1918 inside the armistice with Austria-Hungary of November 3, whose head's source note covers 'the convention infra'; the list gives it a row of its own.

row_subject: Memorandum by the Secretary of StateOpinion that the President’s delay in taking up the matters of organization and apportionment of subjects among the Commissioners is causing confusion and loss of time.
head: Memorandum by the Secretary of State
note: Mr. Lansing's memorandum of January 16, 1919 inside Dr. Young's letter of January 15. Its source is a footnote to its head, not a note of its own: the second shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Memorandum by the Secretary of StateOpinion that a serious mistake is being made in not arranging for a preliminary treaty of peace and a preliminary organization of the League of Nations; comment that the President’s obsession as to a League of Nations blinds him to everything else.
head: Memorandum by the Secretary of State
note: Mr. Lansing's memorandum of March 30, 1919 inside the memorandum of March 27 on the commission's organization. Its source is a footnote to its head, not a note of its own: the second shape #25 describes.

row_subject: Memorandum by the Secretary of StateExpression of profound disapproval of the terms of the peace treaty handed to the German plenipotentiaries on May 7.
head: Memorandum by the Secretary of State
note: Mr. Lansing's memorandum of May 8, 1919 on the treaty's terms inside the memorandum on the commission's personnel, which is dated 'Paris, May 1919' with no day, so that it cannot be shown to be the earlier.

row_subject: President Wilson to the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (Lodge)Transmittal of draft of League of Nations which had been presented to the Conference by the American Commissioners and of formal report of the Commission on the League of Nations; explanation of inability to supply memoranda of debates because of their confidential character.
head: President Wilson to the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (Lodge)
note: President Wilson's letter of August 8, 1919 to Senator Lodge inside the American correspondents' letter of August 5.

row_subject: The Secretary of State to President WilsonAccount of a conversation on May 19 with Mr. Bullitt, who had resigned May 17 because of his objections to the treaty.
head: The Secretary of State to President Wilson
note: Mr. Lansing's letter of September 16, 1919 to the President, in extract, inside the commission's telegram of September 15.

row_subject: President Wilson to the President of the SenateReasons for sending U. S. soldiers to Siberia and explanation of their continuance there.
head: President Wilson to the President of the Senate (Marshall)
note: President Wilson's message of July 22, 1919 to the President of the Senate inside Minister Reinsch's telegram received July 15.

head: Memorandum
